name: Recovery Room Scams
summary: Someone contacts a scam victim promising to recover their lost money for a fee, which is simply a second theft from the same person.

typicalLoss.note: Victims who have already lost heavily are the most willing to pay, which is exactly why they are targeted.

targets: Anyone who has already been scammed
Investment and crypto scam victims in particular

howItWorks.step: They already know you were scammed
howItWorks.detail: Victim lists are traded between criminal groups, so the contact arrives knowing the platform, the amount and sometimes the dates. This specificity is what makes it persuasive.
They present as a blockchain forensics firm, a law firm, an asset recovery agency, or occasionally as regulators or law enforcement.
You are shown a tracing report or told your funds have been located and frozen in a named jurisdiction. The documents are fabricated.
A retainer, then a court filing fee, then a release tax. Structurally identical to the original scam, which is often run by the same people.

redFlags: They contacted you, not the other way around.
Any upfront fee to recover funds.
Claims of a guaranteed recovery, or of funds already located and frozen.
Requests for banking details or ID documents 'to process the return'.
Pressure to act before a court deadline or a freezing order lapses.
illustrativeCase: Four months after losing R190 000 on a fake trading platform, a victim is contacted by a 'digital asset recovery unit' quoting his exact deposit amounts. They send a professional tracing report showing his funds in a Cyprus exchange, pending release on payment of a R38 000 legal retainer. He pays. A R22 000 'jurisdictional clearance fee' follows.
howToProtect: Accept as a rule that no legitimate organisation charges an upfront fee to recover scam losses.
Recognise that anyone who contacts you unprompted about your loss learned about it from the criminals.
Route everything through the SAPS, the FSCA and your bank, none of which charge you.
Be especially careful in the months after a loss, when the desire for a fix is strongest.
Verify any law firm with the Legal Practice Council before engaging.
ifYouveBeenHit: Report to the SAPS, adding it to your existing case if you have one.
Warn others in any victim group you belong to, since these lists circulate widely.
Treat any further approach about your losses as fraudulent by default.

faqs.q: How did they know exactly how much I lost?
faqs.a: Because they either ran the original scam or bought the victim list from whoever did. It is evidence of criminality, not credibility.
Genuine asset recovery exists through courts and regulated insolvency practitioners, usually only for very large or institutional losses. It never begins with a cold call and an upfront fee.
